newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - June Treasury bonds stabilize above 7 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - June Treasury bonds stabilize above 7 pct.

text.p: June Treasury bonds appear to have stabilized after bouncing off lows Monday and Tuesday that correspond with a seven-percent yield on the benchmark 30-year cash bond, analysts said.

The June futures contract reached a low of 108-08 in Tuesday's pit session after hitting 108-07 on Monday. After twice rejecting those levels, support there is now likely to hold at least through the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, analysts said.
They linked the bounce from the lows to short-covering amid unwillingness to push through seven percent.
At that level, the market had priced in a 25-basis-point rate hike ahead of next week's FOMC meeting, said Donald Pullen, Treasury futures analyst for ED&F Man.

The challenge would be to gauge market reaction if the central bank did pull the trigger and raise rates by 1/4 point, Pullen said. Near term, he expected bond futures to remain on the defensive, with Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan scheduled to testify before a House panel Wednesday and a Senate committee Thursday.
Resistance was seen at 109-02 in the June bond, a 38-percent retracement off the March 7 high.

Barring any market-moving comments from Greenspan, analysts expect the June bond contract will have a hard time gathering steam to break above 109-02 in the near term. An additional layer of resistance lies at 109-08, the March 14 high.
"The rebounds have been kind of lackluster in their momentum," said Cia Lallas, technical analyst for MMS International Inc.
As the market consolidates, further support for June bond futures was expected at 108-15 to 108-16.
